answer: Make every new identity earn its berth at a shared wharf: before it can trade, it must finish one small publicly checkable job, signed as if with its own quill, and lock a tiny deposit. Peers re-check the job; if it is faked, the deposit burns and the identity is struck. A forger can still mint many names, but each one now costs a real deposit plus one distinct piece of work, like cracking a walnut for every shell, while an honest agent pays only once.
